rubrics.criterion: The window-to-frame coordinate interpretation (content-rectangle normalization plus all client orientation variants) that the input component currently computes locally is no longer implemented on the input side: the locally duplicated conversion helper is removed and every pointer-processing path (shortcut position query, mouse motion, touch) obtains the mapping from the display side (a restored or equivalently re-homed single owner implementation).
rubrics.rationale: This is the primary displaced calculation of the case: the input component re-implemented a transformation that belongs to the component owning the display geometry.

rubrics.criterion: The geometry decision predicate used by the mouse-button double-click path (whether the click point lies outside the displayed content rectangle) is no longer defined in the input component as a direct reader of the display rectangle fields; the containment decision is reached through the display side.
rubrics.rationale: The border-click resize exclusion is a decision over display-internal geometry; the case deliberately displaced it into the input component as an isolated predicate.

rubrics.criterion: The virtual-finger placement used by the Ctrl/Shift right-click emulation (coordinate conversion followed by inversions against the frame size) is no longer computed inside the input component by reading the display frame size and window state through local helpers; the display-side interpretation is used instead, preserving the exact mirrored/inverted positions and inversion-flag semantics.
rubrics.rationale: This is the composed query of the case: it chains conversion with mirroring over the owner's frame-size state, so repair requires consolidating the chain with its data.

rubrics.criterion: The mouse-capture component no longer inspects display state to decide whether it may consume events: the relative-mode gate that reads through the display object (window handle and the embedded input pipeline's mode flag) is not implemented inside the capture subsystem, and event delegation across the display event loop and the capture handler produces the same accept/forward outcomes as before.
rubrics.rationale: The capture gate duplicated a mode decision the display side already tracks; leaving it in the capture component keeps the two checks synchronized only by hand.

rubrics.criterion: The capture component's collaborator state and initializer signature are consistent with the chosen repair: whatever object the capture subsystem holds (display object or bare window handle), all of its window-manipulating operations reach the window through that single consistent dependency, and the display-side initializer call site matches the signature.
rubrics.rationale: The case widened the capture component's dependency from the window handle to the whole display object; any repair must leave the object graph and both sides of the initializer consistent, not half-migrated.

rubrics.criterion: If display-side state or entry points were consolidated, the client still builds as a whole: headers, forward declarations and call sites on both sides of the input/capture/display boundaries were updated together (no unused declarations left dangling for the consolidated paths, no removed helper still referenced).
rubrics.rationale: The repair spans a struct field change, an initializer signature and several call sites; half-updated collaboration is a concrete failure mode of this instance.

rubrics.criterion: No dead copy of the displaced behavior remains: the input-manager-local conversion helper, the containment predicate, the virtual-finger helper and the capture-side relative-mode gate introduced by the change are all removed or re-homed, and the final source contains exactly one active implementation reachable from all the affected pointer-processing paths.
rubrics.rationale: A repair that only hides the helpers (renames, wraps or re-exposes them unchanged) would leave the misplaced responsibility and its duplication in place.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not merely cosmetically re-inline the same display-state reads: it does not leave the affected pointer-processing paths computing window-to-frame mapping or containment locally by directly reading the display component's rectangle, orientation, content size, frame size, window handle or mode fields from the input or capture components.
rubrics.rationale: For this case, trivially expanding the local helpers back into their call sites reproduces the dispersed responsibility instead of resolving it.

rubrics.criterion: For every client orientation (0, 90, 180, 270 and the flipped variants) the window-to-device coordinate mapping after the repair is identical to before, evaluated on the same content-rectangle and frame-size inputs.
rubrics.rationale: The coordinate math was copied over verbatim; the repair must not lose an orientation case or change integer scaling/rounding behavior, which would inject wrong pointer coordinates on rotated or flipped displays.

rubrics.criterion: The relative-mode event flow does not become double-gated or un-gated: mouse capture does not end up consuming events while the pipeline is not in relative mode, nor forwarding every event when relative mode is active; shortcut-toggle capture, wheel/motion/button consumption rules while active, touch-event consumption, and focus-loss deactivation behave exactly as before the change.
rubrics.rationale: The gate exists on both sides in the injected state; a plausible repair failure is removing one gate but silently changing when the capture handler runs.

rubrics.criterion: The full client test suite passes without new failures, and the repair does not weaken or remove existing tests to make that happen.
rubrics.rationale: The case is explicitly behavior-preserving; modifying tests to accommodate a functional slip is the most likely way a bad repair would hide it.

rubrics.criterion: The repair is not a partial fix: the position query, motion, touch and mouse-button paths, the border-click resize interaction, the virtual-finger emulation and the capture gate are all consolidated; none of the identified manifestations keeps its local display-state reading in the input or capture components.
rubrics.rationale: The task prompt requires a complete repair across the discovered scope; doing only the most visible instance (for example only the coordinate conversion) leaves several manifestations of the same misplaced responsibility behind.
